units.title: Alphabet · Set 1: a, b, t, s, m

objectives.text: say the sound of each letter a, b, t, s and m and match it to its letter
tell that a is a vowel and b, t, s and m are consonants
blend the sounds to read short words like at, am, bat, sat and mat
write the letter for each sound they hear in words like tab and mat

units.title: Alphabet · Set 2: f, c, i, p

objectives.text: say the sounds of f, c (as in cat), i and p and match them to the letters
tell that i is a vowel and f, c and p are consonants
blend the sounds to read short words like it, if, fit, sip and tip
write the letters for the sounds in words like cap, pit and fit

units.title: Alphabet · Set 3: h, l, n, o

objectives.text: say the sounds of h, l, n and o and match them to the letters
tell that o is a vowel and h, l and n are consonants
blend the sounds to read short words like on, not, hot, lot and hop
write the letters for the sounds in words like hit, lap and nap

units.title: Alphabet · Set 4: g, d, r, k

objectives.text: say the sounds of g (as in go), d, r and k and match them to the letters
listen for the first sound in a word and name its letter: g, d, r or k
blend the sounds to read short words like dog, rag, kid, dig and rod
write the letters for the sounds in words like dig, rat and kit

units.title: Alphabet · Set 5: j, v, z, u

objectives.text: say the sounds of j, v, z and u and match them to the letters
tell that u is a vowel and j, v and z are consonants
listen for the first sound in words like jam, van and zip and name the letter
blend the sounds to read short words like jug, up, fun and zip
write the letters for the sounds in words like jog, vat and hug

units.title: Alphabet · Set 6: e, w, y, x, q

objectives.text: say the sounds of e, w, y, x and q, and know q usually comes with u
name all five vowels, a, e, i, o and u, and tell them from consonants
blend the sounds to read short words like wet, yes, box, six and quit
write the letters for the sounds in words like web, fox and yet

units.title: Closed Syllables · CVC & VC Words: Short a

objectives.text: hear and say the short a sound, as in cat, fan and bag
read and spell short a words like cat, fan, bag and map
touch and say each sound, then blend to read words like sat, ham and nap
read short a words in simple sentences, like Sam had a fat cat
read and spell the words can, man, ran, has and was by sight

units.title: Closed Syllables · CVC & VC Words: Short i

objectives.text: hear and say the short i sound, as in fin, big and sit
read and spell short i words like fin, big, sit and lip
tell whether a word has short a or short i, like sat and sit
read short i words in simple sentences, like His pig is big
read and spell the words in, did, him, six and his by sight

units.title: Closed Syllables · CVC & VC Words: Short o

objectives.text: hear and say the short o sound, as in hot, log and rod
read and spell short o words like hot, log, mop and fox
change the vowel to make new words, like hat, hit and hot
read short o words in simple sentences, like Bob got a hot pot
read and spell the words on, got, not and of by sight

units.title: Closed Syllables · CVC & VC Words: Short u

objectives.text: hear and say the short u sound, as in fun, nut and hug
read and spell short u words like fun, nut, hug and bus
tell apart short o and short u in words like hot and hut
read short u words in simple sentences, like Gus can run up to us
read and spell the words up, us, but, run and put by sight

units.title: Closed Syllables · CVC & VC Words: Short e

objectives.text: hear and say the short e sound, as in net, pen and web
read and spell short e words like net, pen, web and bed
tell apart short e and short i in words like pen and pin
read short e words in simple sentences, like Ben has a red pen
read and spell the words let, get, red and yes by sight

units.title: Closed Syllables · CVC Words: All Short Vowels Together

objectives.text: read words with all five short vowels, like cap, bed, pig, hot and sun
read short-vowel sentences aloud smoothly and correctly, rereading to get faster
spell short-vowel words by listening carefully for the middle vowel sound
read and spell words that end in -s, like hits, bugs and wins
find the base word and the ending -s in words like cats and sits
explain that -s can mean more than one, as in bugs and pigs
add -s to action words in sentences, like He runs and Sam sits
read and spell words with sh, like ship, fish and shop
know that s and h together make one sound, as in shed and dish
hear whether sh comes at the start or the end, like ship and wish
read sh words in sentences, like She has a fish in a dish
read and spell the words she and wash by sight
read and spell words with ch, like chop, chin and such
know that c and h together make one sound, as in chip and rich
tell apart ch and sh in words like chip and ship
read ch words in sentences, like Rich can chop a chip
read and spell words with th, like that, math and thin
hear the two th sounds, with the voice on in this and off in thin
read th words in sentences, like Seth did math with them
read and spell the words the, this, then, with and them by sight
read and spell words with wh, like when, whip and which
know that w and h together make one sound at the start of words
read wh question words in sentences, like When is it? What is that?
read and spell the words when, which and what by sight

units.title: Closed Syllables · Consonant Digraphs: Review all

objectives.text: read and spell words with sh, ch, th and wh, like shop, chin, thin and when
sort words by the sound they have: sh, ch, th or wh
read sentences with sh, ch, th and wh words smoothly and correctly
read and spell words that end in -es, like dishes, buzzes and boxes
explain that words ending in s, x, z, sh or ch take -es, not -s
choose -s or -es to make words like cups, foxes and wishes
hear the extra beat that -es adds, as in fox and foxes
read and spell words that start with two consonants, like step, frog and plum
say each sound in a blend, like s-t in stop and f-r in frog
tell a blend like st, where both letters sound, from sh, which is one sound
read beginning-blend words in sentences, like Brad and Fran slip on a slug
read and spell the words and, must, help, stop and from by sight
read and spell words that end with two consonants, like tent, lift and jump
say each ending sound in words like tent (n-t) and jump (m-p)
read ending-blend words in sentences, like The best tent is at the camp
spell words with ending blends by listening for both last sounds, like hand and milk
read short-vowel words with blends, sh, ch and th, like crash, chest and thump
read short stories with these words smoothly, correctly and with expression
spell short-vowel words with blends, sh, ch and th when the teacher says them
read and spell words that end in -ed, like jumped and rested
hear the three sounds of -ed, as in jumped, spelled and rested
explain that -ed tells something already happened, as in Sam jumped
write sentences about yesterday using -ed words, like We camped and fished

units.title: Closed Syllables · Double Consonants: ll, ff, ss, zz

objectives.text: read and spell words ending in ll, ff, ss or zz, like fill, puff, mess and buzz
use the rule: after a short vowel, double a final f, l, s or z
read double-letter words in sentences, like The doll fell off the hill
read and spell the words will, off, well, full and pull by sight
read and spell words ending in ck, like rock, sack and duck
choose ck right after a short vowel (duck) and k after a consonant (milk)
read ck words in sentences, like Jack put a sock in the black box
read and spell the word black by sight
read and spell words ending in tch, like catch, match and itch
choose tch right after a short vowel (catch) and ch otherwise (lunch)
read tch words in sentences, like Mitch can catch and pitch
read and spell the word watch by sight
read and spell words that end in -ing, like jumping, fishing and resting
explain that -ing tells something is happening now, as in Sam is jumping
find the base word in -ing words, like fish in fishing
tell what is happening in a picture with -ing words, like He is kicking

units.title: Closed Syllables · Exceptions: ild, old, ost, ind, olt

objectives.text: read and spell words with ild, ind and old, like wild, kind and fold
read and spell words with ost and olt, like most, post and bolt
know that the vowel in these words says its name, as in find, not fin
read these words in sentences, like The child can hold the cold cup
read and spell the words old, cold, find, hold and mind by sight

units.title: Closed Syllables · -ng and -nk (& new grapheme: ng)

objectives.text: read and spell words with ng, like sing, rang and king
read and spell words with nk, like wink, bank and pink
hear the short i in sing and wink and the short a in rang and bank
read and spell the words bring, thing, think, thank and long by sight
read and spell words with all, like ball, call, tall and wall
use all to spell the ending sound in ball and tall, knowing doll is different
read all words in sentences, like The small ball can fall off the wall
read and spell the words all, fall, small and call by sight
choose c or k to begin words with the k sound, like camp and kit
use the rule: k comes before e, i or y; c comes before other letters
read and spell words like cat, cost, kelp and kid correctly

units.title: Closed Syllables · Digraph & Triple Blends (str, spr, spl, scr)

objectives.text: read and spell words that start with three sounds together, like string, splash and scrap
say each sound in str, spr, spl and scr, like s-t-r in string
read words where sh or th comes before r, like shrub and thrill
read these words in sentences, like Fran split the string and the strap

units.title: Closed Syllables · Morphology Rule: Doubling Rule

objectives.text: read and spell words that double the last letter before -ed or -ing, like rubbed and hopping
explain why hop becomes hopping but jump becomes jumping
add -ed and -ing to words like sit, run and stop, spelling them correctly
read and spell words ending with a vowel that says its name, like me and go
tell the long vowel in go from the short vowel in got
clap and read longer words with an open first part, like ba-by and ro-bot
read and spell the words he, be, so and she, and the tricky words do and to

units.title: Open Syllables · Y as a vowel (long i)

objectives.text: read and spell words where y says long i, like by, my, try and cry
use the rule: English words do not end in i, so we write y, as in sky
read y words in sentences, like Why did the fly cry?
read and spell the words my, by and why by sight

units.title: Open Syllables · Morphology: Drop the y, make it an i

objectives.text: change y to i before adding -es or -ed, as in tries and cried
read and spell words like flies, tried and cries
explain why we write cried but crying, keeping the y before -ing
read and spell words with a and silent e, like cake, game and lake
tell how silent e changes words, like cap to cape and tap to tape
read long a words with silent e in sentences, like Jane ate the cake
read and spell the words make, made, gave, take and came by sight
read and spell words with i and silent e, like fine, smile and bike
change short i words to long i with silent e, like kit to kite and pin to pine
read long i words with silent e in sentences, like Mike rides his bike
read and spell the words like, five, time, ride and white by sight
read and spell words with o and silent e, like home, mole and rope
change short o words to long o with silent e, like hop to hope and not to note
read long o words with silent e in sentences, like The mole dug a hole
read and spell the words those and more, and the tricky words one, some and come
read and spell words with u and silent e, like cube, mule and cute
change short u words to long u with silent e, like cub to cube and tub to tube
read long u words with silent e in sentences, like June has a cute mule
read and spell the words here, these, where and there by sight

units.title: Silent e · VCe Pattern: Review all together

objectives.text: read and spell silent e words with a, i, o and u, like cake, kite, rope and cube
sort words into short and long vowels, like cap and cape, kit and kite
read sentences with silent e words smoothly and correctly
read and spell words where ce says s, like race, mice and face
explain that c says s when e, i or y comes after it, as in rice
read ce words in sentences, like The mice ran a race in a nice place
read and spell the words place, chance and once by sight
read and spell words ending in ge, like page, cage and hinge
read and spell words ending in dge, like bridge, badge and fudge
choose dge right after a short vowel (badge) and ge otherwise (cage)
read and spell the word change by sight
read and spell words ending in ve, like give, have and valve
explain that English words do not end in v, so we add a silent e
notice that the vowel in give and have is short, even with silent e
read and spell the words have, give and live by sight

units.title: Silent e · Morphology: Silent e with suffixes

objectives.text: drop the silent e before adding -ed or -ing, as in raked and hiking
read and spell words like baked, smiling and hoping
tell hoping from hopping, and explain how each word was made
read and write contractions, short words made from two words, like can't and don't
tell which two words make each contraction, like do not in don't
put the apostrophe where letters are left out, as in doesn't and isn't
know that won't is a special one that means will not

units.title: Vowel Teams · Long a: ai, ay

objectives.text: read and spell words with ai, like rain, tail and paint
read and spell words with ay, like stay, play and day
choose ai in the middle of a word (rain) and ay at the end (stay)
read and spell the words play, wait and way, and the tricky words said and they

units.title: Vowel Teams · Long e: ee, ea

objectives.text: read and spell words with ee, like need, feet and green
read and spell words with ea, like seat, eat and leaf
read long e words in sentences, like We eat green beans each week
read and spell the words three, sleep, keep, please and year by sight
add -y to naming words to make describing words, like windy and rainy
read and spell -y words like windy, sunny and dusty
spell sun to sunny and fog to foggy by doubling the last letter
describe the weather with -y words, like It is sunny and windy

units.title: Vowel Teams · Long o: oa, ow, oe

objectives.text: read and spell words with oa, like boat, coat and road
read and spell words with ow and oe that say long o, like slow, snow and toe
choose oa in the middle of a word (boat) and ow at the end (slow)
read and spell the words grow, show, goes and own, and the tricky word though

units.title: Vowel Teams · Long i: igh, ie

objectives.text: read and spell words with igh, like light, night and high
read and spell words with ie, like pie, tie and lie
read long i words in sentences, like The light is on at night
read and spell the words might and right, and the tricky words eye and buy
read and spell words with -ful and -less, like helpful and useless
explain that -ful means full of and -less means without
add -ly to tell how something is done, like quickly and softly
add -ness to make words like sadness, kindness and quickness

units.title: Vowel Teams · Long e: ie; other sounds of ea

objectives.text: read and spell words where ie says long e, like field, chief and piece
read words where ea says short e, like bread and head
read words where ea says long a, like great, steak and break
try another sound for ea when a word does not sound right

units.title: Vowel Teams · Morphology: Prefixes re-, un-

objectives.text: read and spell words with re-, like reread, redo and refill
read and spell words with un-, like unpaid, unlock and unhappy
explain that re- means again or back and un- means not
use re- and un- words to tell what someone did, like She refilled the cup
read and spell words with kn, like knot, knee and knock, where k is silent
read and spell words with wr, like wrist, wrap and wrong, where w is silent
read silent letter words in sentences, like I knew how to tie a knot
read and spell the words know, knew, write and wrote by sight
read and spell words with ar, like star, card and farm
hear how r changes the vowel, as in cat and cart
read ar words in sentences, like The car is parked in the dark
read and spell the words start, part, hard and are by sight
read and spell words with or, like corn, storm and fork
hear how r changes the vowel, as in fox and fork
read or words in sentences, like A horse ran in the storm
read and spell the words for and or, and the tricky words your and four
read and spell words with ir, er and ur, like bird, fern and curb
know that ir, er and ur all make the same sound, as in her
read words with ir, er and ur in sentences, like The first bird hurt her wing
read and spell the words first, her, turn, girl and were by sight
read and spell words with -er and -est, like taller and tallest
use -er and -est to compare, like fast, faster and fastest
explain that -er can also mean a person who, like a farmer or a helper
compare two or three things in a sentence, like My dog is the biggest
read and spell words with war, like war, warm and swarm
read and spell words with wor, like work, word and worm
know w changes the sound: war rhymes with for, and wor sounds like her
read and spell the words warm, world, work and word by sight
read and spell words with -en, like darken, golden and wooden
explain that -en can mean to make, as in darken and soften
explain that -en can mean made of, as in golden and wooden
use -en words in sentences, like The sky will darken at night
read and spell words with oo, like moon, boot and spoon
hear the oo sound in moon and food, and tell it from the o in mop
read oo words in sentences, like Soon the moon will be up
read and spell the words too and soon by sight

units.title: Other Vowels · /ū/ and /yū/: ew, ui, ue

objectives.text: read and spell words with ew, like stew, new and grew
read and spell words with ue and ui, like glue, blue and fruit
hear the two sounds: oo, as in blue, and you, as in few and cue
read and spell the words new, few and blue by sight
read and spell words where oo sounds like book, like look, foot and stood
tell the oo in book from the oo in moon
read these words in sentences, like Look at the good book
read and spell the words good and look, and could, would and should
read and spell words with ou, like house, out and cloud
read and spell words with ow, like cow, how and brown
choose ou at the start or middle (out, loud) and ow at the end (cow)
read and spell the words now, down, our, round and found by sight

units.title: Other Vowels · Morphology: Prefixes pre- and mis-

objectives.text: read and spell words with pre-, like preview, precook and preheat
read and spell words with mis-, like misread, mistake and misspell
explain that pre- means before and mis- means wrong
use pre- and mis- to work out new words, like misplace
read and spell words with oi, like coin, spoil and oil
read and spell words with oy, like toy, boy and joy
choose oi at the start or middle (coin) and oy at the end (toy)
read oi and oy words in sentences, like Roy can point to the toy
read and spell the word boy by sight
read and spell words with aw, like paw, saw and draw
read and spell words with au, like sauce, haul and launch
choose au at the start or middle (sauce) and aw at the end (paw)
read and spell the words saw, draw and cause, and the tricky words caught, laugh and thought
read and spell words with -able, like usable, washable and readable
explain that -able means can be, as in a washable shirt
describe things with -able words, like a breakable cup or a fixable toy

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · Digraphs & ghost sounds: ph, gn, mb

objectives.text: read and spell words with ph, which says f, like phone and graph
read and spell words with gn and mb, like gnaw, sign, thumb and lamb
know that the g in gnaw and the b in thumb are silent
read longer words with these letters, like alphabet, dolphin and climbing
read compound words, two small words joined, like sunset and sandbox
split compound words into their two words, like cup and cake in cupcake
use the two small words to work out the meaning, like a doghouse
make and write new compound words, like rainbow, backpack and goldfish
split two-part words between the two middle consonants, like bas-ket and rab-bit
read and spell two-part words with short vowels, like napkin, muffin and basket
read two-part words in sentences, like The rabbit hid in a basket
read and spell the words until, often and almost by sight
hear the lazy uh sound in words like bacon, data and nickel
know that any vowel can say the lazy uh sound, like the a in sofa
read and spell two-part words with a lazy uh sound, like lemon and wagon

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · Y spells /ē/ & review Suffix -y

objectives.text: read and spell longer words where y at the end says long e, like funny and happy
tell when y says long e (happy) and when it says long i (cry)
add -y to make describing words, like bump to bumpy and fun to funny
read and spell the words only, carry, funny and pretty by sight

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · VCCCV Syllable Division Rule (closed-closed)

objectives.text: split words with three middle consonants, usually after the first, like con-flict
keep blends together when splitting words, like pump-kin and hun-dred
read and spell longer words like pumpkin, hundred, children and monster

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · VCV Words (V-CV and VC-V)

objectives.text: split words with one middle consonant after the vowel for a long sound, like ro-bot
split after the consonant when the vowel is short, like clos-et and cab-in
try both ways to read a new word, like ti-ger or lem-on
read and spell the words even, open, seven, many and along by sight

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · Soft c and Soft G

objectives.text: read words where c says s, like city, pencil and cent
read words where g says j, like gem, giant and magic
use the rule: c and g change their sound before e, i or y
read soft c and g words in sentences, like The giant had a pencil
read and spell words ending in a consonant plus le, like table, turtle and puddle
split -le words right before the consonant, like ta-ble and pud-dle
read -le words in sentences, like The turtle sat by the puddle
read and spell the words little and people by sight

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · 2-Syllable Words with silent e

objectives.text: read and spell two-part words that end with silent e, like explore and define
find the part with silent e and say its long vowel, like fine in define
read these words in sentences, like Kate will invite us to explore the cave
read and spell the words sentence, before and above by sight
read and spell words with -ive, like active, detective and creative
read and spell words ending in tion, which says shun, like action and location
explain that -ion turns a doing word into a thing, like act to action
use -ive words to describe people, like a creative or active friend
read and spell words ending in ture, which says cher, like picture and nature
read and spell words ending in age, which says ij, like package and storage
know that -ure and -age make naming words, like store to storage
use ture and age words in sentences, like I took a picture of the package

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · 2-Syllable Words with Bossy r

objectives.text: read and spell two-part words with ar, or, er, ir or ur, like marker and corner
split words like cor-ner and birth-day, keeping each vowel with its r
read these words in sentences, like My sister has a birthday party
read and spell the words number, under, after, never and mother by sight
read and spell words with ex-, like export, extend and exit
explain that ex- means out, as in export, sending goods out
use ex- to work out new words like exhale and expel

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · 2-Syllable Words with long Vowel Teams

objectives.text: read and spell two-part words with ai, ee, ea, oa and ow, like complain, window and eagle
split words into parts, keeping letter pairs like ai and ow together, as in win-dow
read these words in sentences, like The eagle flew past the window
read and spell the words between, follow, again and ahead by sight

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · Prefixes con, com, in, im

objectives.text: read and spell words with con- and com-, like connect, combine and compare
read and spell words with in- and im-, like invite, incorrect and impossible
explain that con- and com- mean with or together
explain that in- and im- can mean in or not, as in impossible

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · 2-Syllable Words with Vowel Teams (ou, ow, oo, ue, ew, oi, oy, aw)

objectives.text: read and spell two-part words with ou, ow, oo, oi, oy and aw, like about, flower and enjoy
split these words into parts, keeping the vowel letters together, like flow-er and car-toon
read and spell two-part words with ue and ew, like rescue and curfew
read and spell the words because, around and enough by sight
read and spell words with -ment, like treatment, payment and movement
explain that -ment turns a doing word into a thing, like pay to payment
use -ment words in sentences, like We felt excitement at the game
read and spell words with dis-, like dislike, disagree and disappear
read and spell words with de-, like defend, decrease and depart
explain that dis- means not or opposite and de- means off or down
use dis- and de- to work out new words, like dishonest and defrost
read and spell words with -ible, like visible, possible and flexible
explain that -ible, like -able, means can be, as in visible
use -ible words in sentences, like The stars are visible tonight
read and spell words with sub-, like subway, submarine and subtract
read and spell words with trans-, like transport and transform
explain that sub- means under and trans- means across
use sub- and trans- to work out words like subzero and transplant

units.title: Multisyllable & Morphology · Suffix -al/-ial (final stable cial, tial)

objectives.text: read and spell words ending in -al, like dismissal, arrival and personal
read words ending in cial and tial, which say shul, like facial and partial
explain that -al can make describing words, like nature to natural
use -al words in sentences, like Her arrival was a special surprise
